# Tablecloth Trick

> A family table laid with a silk cloth: a tea cup, Mum's bowls, a whole braised fish, Grandma's thermos and the family heirloom. Grab the hem and flick it down. Fast enough and the cloth slides out while everything rattles and stays; too slow and the whole table rides over the edge. Six tables, each harder than the last, and a cat. A tiny cloth-physics toy, no sign-up.

Tablecloth Trick (抽桌布 (zh-CN), El Truco del Mantel (es), Le Coup de la Nappe (fr), テーブルクロス引き (ja)) is a free browser toy at https://yoink.integ.life/ by Integ Life. It opens straight into play: no sign-up, no download, no ads, no tutorial. It works with a mouse or a touchscreen on phones, tablets and computers.

## How to play

1. Put a finger (or the mouse) on the hem of the cloth hanging over the near edge of the table.
2. Flick it down hard and let go. The faster the flick, the less the things on the table move. A slow drag takes everything with it.
3. Perfect means the cloth is off, nothing broke and nothing slid more than 3 cm. Then the next table is laid, with more on it.
4. Table six has the family heirloom on it. A firm pull is not enough there.

## Facts

- URL: https://yoink.integ.life/
- Price: free
- Platforms: any modern web browser (desktop and mobile)
- Languages: English, 简体中文 (Simplified Chinese), Español, Français and 日本語 (Japanese), picked from the browser language (default English)
- Sound: synthesised live with the Web Audio API; vibration on Android
- Made by: Integ Life (https://integ.life/), first published 2026-11-26

## FAQ

**Does the tablecloth trick really work?**
Yes, and this toy simulates why. Friction can only push a dish so hard, so if the cloth leaves quickly enough the dish only gets a short nudge and barely moves. A slow pull gives friction time to drag it along. Silk helps because it is slippery.

**Why did everything fall off?**
The pull was too slow. Below about one metre a second the dishes ride the cloth all the way over the edge. Flick it.

**Why does the heirloom fall over when the bowls are fine?**
It is tall and narrow, so the same tug that slides a bowl a little tips the vase. It needs a faster pull than anything else on the table.

**Is the cat part of the trick?**
The cat does not move. The cloth leaves from under it. Sometimes, afterwards, it pushes a cup off the table anyway; tap the cup to stop it.

**Is Tablecloth Trick free?**
Yes. It is free, with no sign-up, no download and no ads. It runs in any modern browser on phones, tablets and computers.

**Does it have sound and vibration?**
Yes. The hiss of the silk, the clink of each dish and every crash are synthesised live with the Web Audio API; there are no audio files. On Android phones the pull is also felt as ticks of vibration, and a break as a thud.

**Which languages does it support?**
English, 简体中文 (Simplified Chinese), Español, Français and 日本語 (Japanese). The language is picked automatically from your browser settings; any other language falls back to English.

**Who made it?**
Integ Life (integ.life). Tablecloth Trick is one of eleven small stress-relief toys, together with Charge Burst, Void Harvest, Glass Smash, Chain Pop, Knock on Wood, Lap Cat, Squishy Bun, Scratch That, Peel Off, Give It a Twirl. More games are at games.integ.life.

**Is any personal data collected?**
No account and no personal data. At most, anonymous usage statistics (page views and play counts) are collected.
